newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM raises some cargo tariffs ex-Europe.
newsitem.headline: KLM raises some cargo tariffs ex-Europe.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Thursday it planned to raise cargo tariffs on some services from Europe to other regions.

It said the increases -- due to take effect on March 1 1997 -- were driven by the current situation on cargo markets, where competition is fierce. In addition the increases would help defray the costs of technology investments and "steep increases in externally driven costs in the air cargo industry."
Consequently tariffs needed to be raised to a "more economically viable level" in order to ensure continuity of service, KLM said.
It said the tariffs would be independent of the fuel surcharge it announced last year.
"(The) cargo tariff increases are independent of the fuel surcharge of 20 guilder cents per kilogram, or the equivalent in local currency, announced by KLM Cargo last year," KLM said.
The surcharge will continue to be specified separately.
No increases were planned at present for intra-European, African and Central and South American routes, KLM said.
It detailed the planned increase on shipments as follows:
ex-Amsterdam to the Asia Pacific region: 5-10 percent
cities in the area of the Indian sub-continent: 20-30 pct
KLM said it would also be rejigging its European route network of scheduled air freight services, including a rise in the number of non-stop cargo flights.

The changes also include increasing weekly cargo capacity on Amsterdam-Manchester and Amsterdam-Dublin routes, introducing separate services to Linz and Vienna, and launching a new service to Zaragoza in Spain.

In addition the airline will divert its five-times-weekly Amsterdam-Stockholm freight service to Skavsta Airport, some 100 kilometres southwest of Stockholm. This was closer to most of its major customers and would speed up shipments, it said.
